memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Observe my Sabbaths and have reverence for my sanctuary. I am the
LORD'" - Lev 26:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two commands sit side by side: keep the Sabbaths, and revere the
sanctuary. One is about time, the other about place. Together they
shaped how Israel lived — with regular rest and with deep respect for
God's presence.

The Sabbath said: your time belongs to God. The sanctuary said: your
worship belongs to God. Both pushed against the human instinct to treat
everything as ordinary and available for our own use.

Dear reader, reverence is in short supply today. We can be casual about
almost everything, including holy things. We rush into worship
distracted, treat prayer as a formality, and approach God with less care
than we would give an important meeting.

This is not a call to gloomy stiffness. Scripture is full of joyful
worship. But joy and reverence belong together. The writer of Hebrews
urges us to worship God acceptably with reverence and awe, for our God
is a consuming fire (Heb 12:28-29).

Under the New Covenant, the sanctuary is no longer a building. Paul says
our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 6:19), and that we
together are being built into a dwelling for God (Eph 2:22).

Guard your rhythms of rest. Approach God with awe. He is not common, and
neither is time spent with Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I grown casual in how I approach God?
2. Do I guard any real rhythm of rest and worship?
3. How can I recover a sense of reverence this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for treating holy things as ordinary. Restore in me
reverence for You and a healthy rhythm of rest, and let me worship You
with awe. Amen.
